title: How long a window of sound does it take to sync two drifting cameras, and how often must you redo it?
summary: Synthetic speech-like audio (shared source, independent noise, optional reverb), per-window GCC-PHAT delay (100–4000 Hz) and a Theil–Sen line over 12 windows in 1 h at 40 ppm clock error. With 2 s windows the fit is below 0.02 ms from −10 dB SNR up and fails completely at −15 dB; 5 s windows hold to −15 dB. A sync made once at the start drifts one 30 fps frame (33.3 ms) in 833 s at 40 ppm (144 ms after an hour; analytic ppm × time reproduced exactly). Reverb at −10 dB direct-to-reverberant adds 4adds 4–8 msndash;5 ms (median). Not from real recordings: the audio and the exact delay are synthetic and the ppm values are swept, none sourced (no datasheet reachable).
lede: how long a window of sound syncs two drifting cameras? GCC-PHAT plus a robust line fit syncs to under 0.02 ms over an hour from -10 dB SNR with 2 s windows; a sync made once at the start drifts one frame in 833 s at 40 ppm.
